meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties concluded with non-EU states
Luxembourg double taxation treaty network, including the Luxembourg–United States income and capital tax treaty (1996)
EU Treaty provisions on freedom of establishment and free movement of capital (TFEU Arts. 49 and 63)
OECD/Council of Europe Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (as applied by Luxembourg)
OECD BEPS Multilateral Instrument (MLI) as ratified by Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the 2013 reform introducing the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 February 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Luxembourg Business Registers, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney executed by each general partner or authorized signatory for incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization if the issuer is not party to the 1961 Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing and board resolution of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry / competent corporate registry of the general partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certified copies of passports or national identity documents of all partners identified as beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry/passport authority of the document holder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled criminal record certificate (casier judiciaire) for each individual general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or criminal-records authority of the partner's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every general partner, limited partner with 25% or more interest, beneficial owner, signatory and POA holder against EU Council consolidated financial sanctions, OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, UN Security Council sanctions, Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and CSSF AML/CFT lists, and commercial PEP databases; PEP status of the individual and close associates/family triggers enhanced due diligence under the amended Law of 12 November 2004. Any hit, unusual transaction or elevated-risk finding must be escalated to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) in accordance with statutory reporting obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are in French, German or Luxembourgish; the corporate name must be in Latin script. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RCS, and the registered legal form suffix must be 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying sovereign or public connection ('Luxembourg State', 'Government', 'Ministère', 'Commune') – require prior ministerial or communal authorization
Regulated financial terms ('Bank', 'Banque', 'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Pension', 'Fund', 'Bourse/Exchange') – require prior CSSF or CAA license/clearance
Statutorily protected institutional names ('Chamber of Commerce', 'University', 'Red Cross', 'Bar Association')
Legal-form suffixes misrepresenting the entity type (e.g., 'S.A.', 'S.à r.l.', 'SARL', 'SCS' for an SCSp)
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a rejection, request written reasons from the RCSL/LBR registrar; if the objection persists, file a recours en annulation with the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification, attaching the refusal letter and corrected name evidence. Sensitive-token refusals may be cured by obtaining the relevant CSSF/CAA or ministerial authorization. A valid reservation may be renewed through the LBR portal before expiry; otherwise the name is released.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a licensed Luxembourg registered-office/domiciliation agent with a physical office that can receive inspection visits. A pure virtual mailbox without physical substance does not satisfy the statutory seat requirement of Article 1 of the Law of 10 August 1915, nor Luxembourg tax substance expectations; the SCSp must maintain a genuine Luxembourg seat where management decisions, books and records are accessible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for a passive electronic-components distribution SCSp; estimated annual unannounced physical inspection probability is below 10% absent tax, UBO or AML red flags, but materially increases if the entity claims tax treaty benefits or is involved in intra-group financing or high-risk jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), together with the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); SCSp provisions set out at Articles 118 et seq., including formation, contribution, management, registration and publication rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, “RCS”), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (“LBR”); electronic filing through guichet.lu and the LBR portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership deed and registration declaration (contrat de société et déclaration d’enregistrement au registre de commerce et des sociétés), followed by mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (“RESA”).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; no statutory escrow account or notarial capital deposit is required. The amount and timing of contributions are freely set out in the partnership agreement. At least one general partner with unlimited liability and one limited partner whose liability is limited to their contribution must exist.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partnership deed of the SCSp is approved and the subscription amounts and contributions of the general partner and limited partners, as set forth in the subscription schedule, are accepted. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, and the General Partner is authorised to engage a registered agent and arrange bank accounts. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Manager (gérant) of the SCSp, with authority to register the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, publish the required legal filing, sign tax and social security registrations, open bank accounts, and complete all necessary incorporation steps. RESOLVED, that all actions taken in connection with the formation before the date hereof are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online search and guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an RCS name search to confirm availability. The name must contain 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' and must not conflict with existing legal names. Submit a name availability request through the LBR portal or via a Luxembourg public notary; acceptance of the name is not a formal reservation unless a notarial deed is subsequently executed within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
Passport or national ID of the proposed general partner or signatory
Brief description of the intended corporate purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict or non-distinctiveness, file an alternative name through LBR without penalty. If the LBR requests further clarification, respond through guichet.lu within 15 days; no new fee applies for a revised name verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties acting in person or through a Luxembourg notary; notarial form is optional for SCSp formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership deed containing the exact corporate name, registered office address, duration, corporate purpose, identity of general and limited partners, contribution amounts, capital accounts, management powers of the gérant, profit and loss allocation, and Luxembourg governing-law clauses. Execute the deed by all partners; if a notary is used, the notary will verify identity and capacity and retain the original for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership deed in French or with certified translation
Subscription and contribution schedule
Passport or ID and proof of address of each partner
Beneficial ownership declaration (for AML/KYC purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects or requests amendments to the deed, execute an amending private deed or notarial deed and refile the restated partnership agreement. Corrective filings do not restart the underlying registration once the original deed is legally valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and legal entry into force
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership deed and the RCS registration form electronically through guichet.lu/LBR. Attach all required documents and certified translations if applicable. LBR examines the file, assigns the RCS number, and registers the SCSp; legal effects against third parties begin once registration and required publication occur.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed
Standard RCS registration form
Identity documents of the gérant and all partners
Power of attorney, if the filing is made by a representative
Proof of registered office availability (lease, address confirmation letter, or notarial attestation)
Beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If LBR issues a completeness notice or query, respond within the notified period with the missing annexes or clarifications. If registration is unjustifiably refused, appeal the decision before the Luxembourg courts within one month of written refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and obtainment of official RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, LBR publishes the registered partnership deed excerpt and the public register metadata in RESA. Download the official RCS extract and confirm the effective registration date, RCS number, and correctness of the legal form and registered office details.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Registered partnership deed as approved by RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, request rectification through LBR by filing a corrected extract or an explanatory amending statement. An administrative delay beyond 30 days may be escalated to LBR supervisory services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDV); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp with the AEDV for VAT and with the ACD for income and business tax identification to the extent applicable. Because the SCSp lacks separate legal personality and is generally fiscally transparent, ensure that all partners are identified for tax assessment. Open the employer file with CCSS before hiring any staff and fulfill the filing of the annual social declaration. Submit the general statistics registration if required by the National Institute of Statistics.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and RESA publication confirmation
Executed partnership deed
Beneficial ownership and partner identification forms
Tax residency certificates of partners if claiming treaty or transparency treatment
Registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDV delays VAT registration, file a manual VAT registration request and escalate to the taxpayer service. If CCSS disputes the employer status, submit a declaration of no employees or postpone registration until the first hire; appeal administrative decisions within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and AML/KYC activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Luxembourg credit institution or EEA-authorized bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation dossier to the bank and complete the bank’s client onboarding, AML/KYC, and source-of-funds questionnaires. Open the SCSp bank account in the partnership name and configure payment rails for SWIFT wire transfers and credit-line facilities once the creditworthiness assessment is completed.
required_dossiers: Official RCS extract and RESA publication
Executed partnership deed
Beneficial ownership register and declaration
Passport and proof of address of all partners and the manager
Source of funds and source of wealth statement
Bank account signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank makes a KYC referral, provide additional source-of-funds documentation or legal-entity chart within the bank’s requested period. If refused, apply to another credit institution; the unchanged tax and legal status of the SCSp remains unaffected by any banking refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l’Économie – Direction générale de l’industrie et de l’artisanat (notification only; no industrial operating permit is required for wholesalers of passive electronic components under ISIC 4652)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – wholesale distribution of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors is a non-regulated commercial activity in Luxembourg; no manufacturing license, sectoral authorization, or import/export permit applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA registration or full environmental impact assessment is required for ordinary warehousing and distribution of passive electronic components. A registration under environmental legislation would only be triggered if hazardous substance storage thresholds, combustion plant, refrigerant installations, or significant wastewater discharges exist.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing discharge or VOC release points exist in the passive component trade. Sanitary wastewater must comply with the municipal drainage regulation and the applicable grand-ducal wastewater standards. If HVAC or refrigeration equipment is installed, the SCSp must comply with Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases; generated waste is managed under municipal waste rules and the WEEE Directive if discarded electronic components are treated as waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the registered office/warehouse must be obtained from the Inspection du Service d’Incendie et de Secours (ISIS) where premises are leased for storage. Structural load verification is required for racked warehouses and must be confirmed by the landlord’s structural engineer or an approved Luxembourg bureau de contrôle. Occupational safety clearance is ensured under the Labour Code by conducting a workplace risk assessment, appointing an external accident-prevention service, and providing mandatory staff training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority – for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority – for income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; unified electronic filing portal: MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the foreign SCSp structure creates Luxembourg nexus: VAT registration is required as soon as any taxable activity is commenced in Luxembourg, whereas direct-tax registration is required only where a Luxembourg permanent establishment, real estate, or payroll presence exists. Step 2: Appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative unless the foreign entity is established in the EU/EEA or in a jurisdiction with which Luxembourg has concluded mutual administrative assistance and recovery arrangements. Step 3: File the Luxembourg VAT registration application (déclaration d'immatriculation à la TVA, Formulaire 102) electronically via MyGuichet.lu, signed by the general partner/managers. Step 4: Attach the foreign certificate of incorporation, excerpt from the home-country trade register, proof of identity of the general partner, and the VAT representative mandate. Step 5: The AEDT issues the national VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits and, where applicable, the ACD attributes a Luxembourg national identification number for direct-tax and social security purposes; the entity is inserted into the Luxembourg VAT register with effect from the registration date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax purposes by default: no corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax is levied at entity level, and partners are taxed in their own hands on their profit shares. Statutory elections available: (1) under Article 182bis LIR, the SCSp may validly elect to be taxed as a capital company (option pour le régime des sociétés de capitaux), thereby becoming subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the election is binding for a statutory minimum period. (2) The SCSp may form or join a Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) with related taxable persons, making the group a single VAT taxpayer. (3) The transparency default may be overridden under the ATAD hybrid mismatch rules where the same payment would otherwise produce dual inclusion or non-inclusion mismatch, requiring neutralisation at the partners' level. (4) The small-business VAT franchise exemption may be declined in favour of ordinary VAT taxation with input VAT recovery.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) – EU VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (net annual turnover) for the small-business franchise exemption available to established Luxembourg taxable persons; no registration threshold applies to non-established foreign entities, which are registrable from the first euro of Luxembourg taxable turnover. For EU distance sales of goods to Luxembourg consumers: EUR 10,000 pan-EU harmonised threshold. An SCSp actively distributing electronic components will ordinarily exceed the franchise threshold and is therefore required to register for Luxembourg VAT from the date the threshold is exceeded or, where the option for ordinary taxation is exercised, from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently operates no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime for domestic B2B invoices. Mandatory e-invoicing applies to B2G invoices addressed to the Luxembourg central government, which must be submitted in structured electronic format over the PEPPOL network. Periodic VAT e-returns must be accompanied, for medium and large taxpayers and certain high-risk sectors, by SAF-T digital accounting files (fichier d'échange), enabling AEDT analytical cross-matching of invoices, customs declarations and payment flows. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) legislative package will, upon transposition, introduce mandatory e-invoicing and transaction e-reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies on the EU-wide statutory timeline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods (excess multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors falling under ECCN 8542) physically exported outside the EU are zero-rated at 0% VAT (exempt with credit). The zero rate is conditional on: (1) the supply being directly linked to dispatch or transport by the supplier, or on the supplier's behalf, to a destination outside the EU customs territory; (2) export departure being completed within the statutory period (goods must leave the EU within 90 days); (3) the supplier holding complete documentary proof of physical removal before claiming the zero rate. Intra-EU B2B dispatches are likewise zero-rated where the customer's VAT ID is valid under VIES and the recapitulative statement is filed. Services connected to exported goods and rendered to non-EU business customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rules, preserving direct or pro-rata input VAT recovery. No special export licence applies to EAR99 electronic components absent dual-use diversion risks.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic Single Administrative Document with Movement Reference Number) issued by Luxembourg or EU customs at export clearance
Commercial invoice, packing list and Incoterms 2020 contract evidencing exporter, consignee, quantity, unit prices and foreign destination
Transport title: ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR international consignment note proving physical delivery outside the EU customs territory
Warehouse release and removal records for the passive electronic inventory, together with customs exit confirmation
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT MT103 bank settlement evidence demonstrating collection of export proceeds and FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT cross-matches zero-rated sales declared in VAT returns against actual customs export declarations (MRN database) and bank inflows; any inconsistency or missing documentation triggers reassessment of the turnover at the standard 17% VAT rate, disallowance of connected input VAT credit, and issuance of an enforceable assessment with monthly default interest. Administrative penalties of up to EUR 250,000 apply, and late-filing surcharges accrue from the statutory due date. Deliberate fabrication of export documents, sham foreign counterparties, circular export schemes and fraudulent repatriation structures engage the criminal tax-fraud provisions of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), attracting fines and imprisonment, joint and several liability of the general partner and the appointed VAT representative, and retrospective clawback for up to 10 years in cases of established fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; no separate foreign-exchange control administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in a Euro-area economy. Luxembourg maintains no general exchange-control regime; the euro is the domestic currency and is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Capital movements, dividend distributions, profit repatriation, and capital repayment are unrestricted under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC. The legal basis for the SCSp being fiscally transparent means profit remittances to partners are generally treated as allocations rather than dividend distributions, mitigating Luxembourg dividend withholding tax exposure. Operational hurdles remain only in the form of AML/KYC documentation and, where applicable, statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio into euros, and no explicit repatriation timeline. Export receipts denominated in foreign currency may be retained, converted, or disbursed freely. The BCL requires only statistical balance-of-payments declarations for direct investment and trade flows, not advance approval or conversion mandates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Credit Line Collateral Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions authorized by the CSSF under the Law of 27 July 2018 may provide payment accounts and remote onboarding, but they generally cannot provide SWIFT MT103 treasury clearing, TARGET2 direct access, or commercial credit lines. Non-EU offshore EMIs are not viable as primary treasury rails because they lack SEPA participation, TARGET2 settlement, and CSSF oversight. The recommended use of an EMI is limited to low-balance operational float; capital escrow and trade disbursements should be routed through a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of at least one authorised signatory (normally the general partner or a fully empowered director) and of the ultimate beneficial owner(s) is the prevailing practice at BCEE, BIL, and BGL BNP Paribas. CSSF AML frameworks (notably CSSF Regulation 18/698 and the Law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners) permit remote video identification under defined conditions, and certain institutions allow fully remote opening using Luxembourg eID (LuxTrust). However, for a passively held SCSp with no employees and a multi-layered UBO chain, the bank’s risk-based approach will in practice mandate either a physical interview or an enhanced video conference with notarised attestation. Recommendation: arrange physical sign-off for the initial onboarding and use a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent to bridge ongoing KYC communications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bare passive structure with no employees, no independent substance, and classification as an 'other financial vehicle' under Luxembourg KYC typologies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated partnership agreement of the SCSp, RCS extract, non-public participation register excerpt, general partner CV and professional track record, substance documentation including registered office lease, domiciliation agreement, letter from the Luxembourg tax administration confirming the tax status, and an economic-purpose memorandum describing the physical distribution of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: limited partners are not publicly registered and beneficial ownership chain extends to non-EU ultimate principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial owner declaration filed with the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), chain-of-title waterfall chart, passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds affidavits, notarised sub-trust declarations, and evidence of direct investor control over distributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Electronic components trade flows inconsistent with stated passive inventory model; invoice or counterparty documentation mismatch
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, purchase orders, packing lists, Incoterms 2020 terms, transport documentation (CMR, bill of lading, airway bill), warehouse receipts evidencing physical inventory location, insurance certificates, and a 12-month purchase and sales register matching the ISIC 4652 distribution scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed credit line or overdraft facility disproportionate to the entity's net asset value, with unexplained transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or sufficiently documented financial statements, 12-month treasury forecast, receivable and payable ageing schedule, MLCC and resistor inventory turnover model, ownership and guarantee structure, list of primary counterparties, sanctions and PEP screening results, and an independent valuation of the passive inventory collateral.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction mismatch: settlement routing via intermediary offshore banks or counterparty banks not directly participating in European clearing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct TARGET2 and SEPA settlement chart showing no offshore relay, confirmation that all counterparty banks are BCL-direct, SEPA-member, or SWIFT-KYC-registered institutions, end-beneficiary declarations, and a funds-flow narrative aligning each inbound and outbound payment to the underlying trade invoice.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the contributing partner's bank to the SCSp's euro IBAN reference account. The payment narrative must clearly indicate 'capital contribution' and cite the applicable clause of the SCSp partnership agreement under the Luxembourg Law on Commercial Companies of 10 August 1915, as amended. No Luxembourg exchange-control approval or prior BCL authorisation is required, but statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL may apply. For inbound wires exceeding EUR 10,000 from non-EU jurisdictions, banks will require source-of-wealth evidence, a contribution resolution signed by the general partner, an updated subscription schedule, and confirmation that the funds are non-taxable capital in nature rather than trading revenue.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement is structured through (a) SEPA credit transfers for euro-denominated supplier invoices within the SEPA zone, (b) SWIFT MT103 (opc) high-value international wires for non-euro supplier payments via TARGET2 or correspondent clearing, and (c) irrevocable commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600 for large procurement contracts of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors from Asian manufacturers. Documentary collections and sight drafts are used for lower-risk open-account trade. Disbursements are matched against purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, and warehouse receipts; foreign exchange conversion is executed at the bank's institutional clip through the Luxembourg account-holding bank rather than a retail FX desk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/JPY outright forwards with tenors up to 12 months documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) used for rolling inventory procurement exposure in EUR/USD
Plain vanilla currency options (EUR call/put, cash-settled) under a bank FX Master Agreement for hedging forecast procurement denominated in USD and JPY
Cross-currency swaps limited to risk-reduction of committed inventory supply contracts where a genuine underlying trade exposure is demonstrable

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-deliverable emerging-market currencies, as risk-reduction instruments strictly subordinated to documented trade payables, subject to bank internal counterparty-credit approval and CSSF derivative-capital guidance; euro deliverable forwards remain the standard hedging route

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: filed at least once per calendar year through the RBE online portal and within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 35,000 for late filings; criminal penalties for false declarations; persistent default may trigger dissolution or strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and publication (comptes annuels), if statutory thresholds apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) eJusticia portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end for approval; RCS filing and publication within 1 month of approval and no later than 8 months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS late-filing penalty of EUR 50 per day with a cap applied by the Public Prosecutor; court-ordered compliance and possible administrative strike-off after sustained non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal) for commercial SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and communal tax collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year filers: by 31 December of the year following the tax year; fiscal-year filers: by the anniversary of the tax year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; official tax assessment and penalty surcharge up to 10% for failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) for SCSp carrying on commercial activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the following year for calendar-year entities, or by the anniversary of the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest of 0.6% per month and penalty surcharges; incomplete filing can result in official valuation assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also required if the SCSp is classified as a public-interest undertaking or is otherwise subject to the publication obligations of the Law of 10 August 1915 and exceeds the relevant size criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 2009; IFRS is permitted or required where the entity is a securities issuer or prepares consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain accurate beneficial ownership records in the RBE register. Any transfer of limited or general partnership interests must be reported within 30 days. Annually, the general partner or registered agent must confirm through the RBE portal that the beneficial ownership information remains current and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners recording contributions, transfers, redemptions, and voting rights
Register of general partners and managers with acceptance and removal records
Minute book containing partner resolutions, management decisions, and annual accounts approval

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level due to fiscal transparency; 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg corporate income tax for resident corporate partners in Luxembourg City (17% national CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level corporate income tax; no statutory tax holiday for component distribution; profit is allocated to partners and taxed only at partner level; corporate partners may apply the Luxembourg participation exemption on qualifying distributions and the notional interest deduction, subject to ATAD interest limitation rules; 80% participation exemption is not available for trading inventory profits
